macro_context.market_sentiment: Cautiously risk-on on May 5: S&P 500 +0.78%, Nasdaq +0.90%, Dow +0.52% as markets partially recovered from the May 4 sell-off triggered by UAE intercepting Iranian missiles. Oil remains elevated (WTI ~$104/bbl, Brent ~$113/bbl), but easing slightly from Monday's spike. Source: TheStreet, Bloomberg (May 5 2026).
macro_context.fed_outlook: Fed held rates at 3.50-3.75% on April 29, 2026 in a contentious 8-4 vote — the widest dissent since Oct 1992. Three members dissented hawkishly (wanted to remove rate-cut language); one Trump appointee dissented dovishly (wanted immediate cut). Powell remains on the board despite political pressure; his successor as chair is pending. No cuts expected in 2026 given elevated energy-driven inflation. Source: CNBC, Federal Reserve (Apr 29 2026).
macro_context.geopolitical: Active US-Iran conflict is the dominant risk: UAE intercepted Iranian missiles May 4 (first activation since ceasefire began last month), sending oil surging and equities lower. Strait of Hormuz closure risk is cited by IMF as a tail scenario. Additional flashpoints: Venezuela unrest, NATO posture in Greenland. IMF baseline projects 3.1% global growth, 4.4% inflation for 2026; adverse scenario 2.5%/5.4%. US tariff uncertainty and midterm elections add to macro uncertainty. Source: Motley Fool, IMF WEO April 2026.

analyst_consensus.recent_changes: Evercore ISI maintained Outperform with $340 PT on April 17, 2026. TD Cowen raised PT to $375 (Buy). Wolfe Research downgraded from Outperform to Peerperform on Jan 7, 2026, citing slower EPS growth vs peers due to asset sensitivity and higher expense growth. Overall: 33 analysts, 14 Buy / 12 Hold / 0 Sell; median PT $345, range $289-$400. Source: Benzinga, MarketBeat, Investing.com.

competitor_activity: Goldman Sachs posted record Q1 equities trading revenue (EPS $17.55, +14.4% YoY), outpacing JPM's investment banking growth and putting pressure on JPM's market share in equities. Wells Fargo, freed from its asset cap, is entering the options clearing market and launching premium credit cards — its business mix increasingly resembles JPM's, heightening retail and commercial banking competition. Bank of America is aggressively cross-selling wealth management, directly targeting JPM's private client franchise. All big banks beat Q1 estimates, suggesting the sector is broadly performing well, but Wall Street remains cautious on credit quality given the geopolitical/energy headwinds. Source: American Banker, Yahoo Finance, Chronicle Journal.
